external_spec_note: The correct grouping (P distributing over both cross terms t*B and T*b before dividing by 2*T*B) is derivable from ordinary algebra applied to the function's own operands and the in-function values already in scope; no protocol/business convention beyond the source is needed.
extraction_note: Attached at the buggy statement `uint _units = (((P * part1) + part2) / part3);` (case JSON line 40 / original .sol line 46), inside the else branch of `if(P == 0){ return b; } else { ... }`. Debug seeds (b=t=100, B=T=1000, P=500) confirm the discrimination: part1=t*B=100000, part2=T*b=100000, part3=(T*B)*2=2,000,000; buggy _units=(500*100000+100000)/2,000,000=25 vs intended _units=500*(100000+100000)/2,000,000=50 (matches annotation_plans.md's stated 25-vs-50, consulted only for background/cross-check, not for annotation text, per instructions - no discrepancy found). Judgment calls: (1) excluded the `if(P==0)` branch condition from relevant_statements as a pure reachability/branch-selection gate - it doesn't redefine any value the relation depends on, it only determines whether the annotated else-branch executes at all, same as README's require()-exclusion example; (2) counted part1/part2/part3's three definition statements as relevant even though the relation text inlines them (t*B, T*b, (T*B)*2) rather than naming them by identifier, because their definitions are necessary context to confirm the annotation is the correctly-grouped restatement of the same quantities the buggy line computes - this is the disputed statement's own necessary supporting context, not the barred self-substitution-as-evidence pattern (the disputed statement `_units = (P*part1+part2)/part3` itself is also counted, per the same rule); (3) Value-level: the bug is a missing-parentheses/wrong-grouping defect - all three operations (multiply by P, sum the two cross terms, divide by 2*T*B) are present in the buggy code, just mis-grouped so P fails to distribute over the second cross term; no distinct processing step is missing, so this is Value-level (not Algorithm-level) per SS5's classification principle, analogous to `web3bugs_60_H_01`'s wrong/extra-operand pattern. No disagreement with annotation_plans.md's background description (missing-parentheses bug, same pattern as 5_H_07) found.
